By Yihui XieNovember 7, 2026 at 2:26 AM UTCBookmark

China’s central bank added to its gold reserves in October — extending a buying streak to two years — as the precious metal fell almost 7% to end the month below the $4,000-an-ounce support threshold.
Bullion holdings at the People’s Bank of China rose by 830,000 ounces in October, or around 25.8 metric tons, according to official data released Saturday. That’s the 24th consecutive month of accumulation. In particular, the central bank has stepped up purchases in recent months as gold prices have slumped, with additions in the first 10 months of the year totaling around 129 metric tons.

China strongly opposes US sanctions on two Chinese companies over their dealings with a third party and reserves the right to take “necessary measures” to protect its interests, China’s Ministry of Commerce said on Saturday.
Beijing said the US recently stepped up sanctions and imposed multiple “discriminatory” restrictions on China, damaging the rights of local companies and undermining stability in economic and trade relations. It urged Washington to “correct its wrong practices” as soon as possible.

Sweetgreen CEO Says Sales Rebound After Cyclospora-Related Traffic Drop

The company reported October comparable sales growth of about 5%, following a return to flat comps in September, and saw further improvement in early November. item.title: FIGS Beats Earnings as Demand Outstrips Supply, CEO Trina Spear Says
item.description:
Nov 6th, 2026
FIGS Beats Earnings as Demand Outstrips Supply, CEO Trina Spear Says
FIGS reported third-quarter top- and bottom-line results above expectations, with revenue of $190.7 million versus an estimate of $182.8 million. The company logged a fourth consecutive quarter of at least 25% revenue growth; non-scrubwear revenue rose 35%, and international revenue also increased. CEO and co-founder Trina Spear said health care professionals are expanding their FIGS purchases beyond scrubs to items such as underscrubs, compression socks and outerwear, for work and off-duty wear. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Kailey Leinz on "The Close."

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Talks between Brazil’s Braskem SA and its creditors regarding an out-of-court debt rework have soured, with shareholders taking a proposed capital injection key to a deal off the table if talks stand as they are, according to people familiar with the matter.
After meetings with creditors in New York this week, shareholders decided to go back on a pledge to inject capital into Braskem after bondholders rejected a proposal that included $3.8 billion in debt conversion, the people said, asking not to be named discussing private matters. Negotiations are still ongoing and no final decision has been made.

item.title: AI-Generated Movie Heading Theaters
item.description:
BusinessWeek Radio Simulcast • Nov 6th, 2026
AI-Generated Movie Heading Theaters
Artificial intelligence is moving from experimental videos to the big screen. Fable Studio CEO Edward Saatchi says a team of just 30 people spent nine months creating Gods Don’t Give Gifts, an AI-generated animated feature that still relies on human directors, writers, voice actors and artists. He joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss how AI changes the filmmaking process and what it means for Hollywood's traditional production model.
